style_reason: Wheels, rails, sleepers and ballast are physical, layered objects; a cut-paper diorama lets the viewer see a train from impossible angles (under the coach, along the axle, from above the bend) while staying warm and tactile. Exaggerated paper cones make an invisible, slight taper visible.

story.idea: A heavy train swings round a hillside bend with no steering wheel; a girl at the fence wonders why it does not slide off.
Most people credit the inner rim (flange); the real secret is the wheel shape.
Two wheels are fixed on one rigid axle and always turn together.
Each tread is slightly coned like an ice-cream cone: fat on the inside, thin on the outside.
If the wheelset drifts sideways, the slope brings it back to the middle by itself.
On a bend the set shifts outward; the outer wheel rides its fat part and covers more distance per turn.
The inner wheel rides its thin part and covers less; so the train follows the bend without slipping.
The flange is the last line of defence against strong pushes like crosswinds; the real work is done by the small slope.

motifs.stands_for: the coned tread (an ice-cream cone; fat inside, thin outside)
the flange, the backup rim (marked in terracotta)
distance travelled per wheel turn (paper measuring tape: orange long, blue short)
the viewer's curiosity; opens with the question and closes with the answer
the middle of the track (a chalk centre mark)

assets.description: cut-paper monsoon hillside: layered hills, tea terraces, waterfall, palms, curving track
2.5D paper train (locomotive and coaches) drawn along the curve
girl in a school uniform, three-quarter view, jointed paper puppet with expressions
track-level view beside a coach: bogie frame, springs, wheel disc, rail, sleepers, ballast
view along the track: wheelset front view, rails in cross-section, sleepers converging to fields
workshop wall: pegboard tools, window light, blueprint of the wheel profile, bench with a chai glass
paper ice-cream cone with a scoop
top-down bend: fields, trees, hut roofs, curved track and wheelset seen from above
paper fibres and tile textures from the Paper Explainer kit

guardrails: no numbers for weight, speed, taper or wheel size
the taper is exaggerated in all art and called slight in narration
the flange is the backup, never shown as the main guide
straight-track self-centring is shown only as drift and return, without more mechanism detail than the sources give
train, track and landscape are illustrative, not a specific railway
